_comment: What this bundle ships and which gates it can decide by itself. kind 'scan' means a script here answers it when pointed at a project root; kind 'suite' means the bundle names the rule but the project has to write its own test — those are reported as pending, never as passed. Some shipped files are neither: gates_doctor.py, preflight.py, lint_commits.py and check_issue_handoff.py are tools a project runs with context only its CI has (a commit range, a pull request number), so they take flags rather than a root and the doctor does not run them. The rules they enforce are published in rules.yaml like any other.

actions-sha-pinned.title: Every action is pinned to a commit SHA with the version in a comment

adr-index-complete.title: The ADR index covers every record, numbered without repeats or gaps · and supersessions are recorded in both directions

ci-tools-hash-pinned.title: Tools CI installs for itself are pinned by hash, on both the Python and the Node side

csp-no-inline.title: CSP is pure self — no inline script, style, or handler anywhere

delete-means-soft-delete.title: Delete means hide (soft delete) — only purge removes rows for real

gates-registry-total.title: The gate index matches reality in both directions, and every test file is accounted for

image-digest-pinned.title: The base image is pinned to a manifest-index digest and Dependabot moves it

logic-knows-no-http.title: All logic lives in the service layer and knows nothing about HTTP

no-debug-entrypoint.title: No entrypoint file can open a debug console, even when the wrong one is run

_requires_why: Shipped files are stdlib-only so they run in a project that has installed nothing. preflight.py is the exception: it reads whole workflow files, which the narrow subset reader in the scans cannot do, and it runs on a developer's machine rather than a bare CI runner. The dependency is declared here so a target project learns it from the bundle instead of from a traceback, and a test holds this list to what the files actually import.
